description: Hand-curated Java methods stratified by lexical false-positive source type. Designed to surface and measure the FP class addressed by strip_java_lexical_noise (F10).
stratification: 30 cases = 5 fp_source_types x 6 cases (5 negatives + 1 positive per type). Negatives verify F10 eliminates the FP. Positives verify F10 does not over-strip active code that legitimately contains the same token.

cases.rationale: MD5 appears only inside a // comment; the active code uses SHA-256. (MessageDigest the class is imported and called with SHA-256 in active code, so it isn't a noise-exclusive token.)

The // comment contains the full SQL-injection FP-triggering pattern: stmt.executeQuery("SELECT ... " + req.getParameter("id")). Pre-F10 the comment would induce the SQL rule to fire; post-F10 the comment is stripped and the active code uses parameter-bound prepareStatement.
new Random( appears only inside a // TODO comment; the active code uses SecureRandom.

The // comments contain the full CMD-injection FP-triggering pattern: ProcessBuilder + .command + Runtime.getRuntime().exec + concat + req.getParameter. Pre-F10 the comment would induce the CMD rule to fire; post-F10 the comments are stripped and the active code returns a constant.

The // comment contains the full XPath-injection FP-triggering pattern: XPathFactory.newInstance().newXPath().compile + concat + req.getParameter + .evaluate. Pre-F10 the comment would induce the XPath rule to fire; post-F10 the comment is stripped and the active code returns a static label.
MD5 appears in a // comment AND the active code uses MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5"). F10 must not strip the active call.
MD5 appears only inside javadoc; the active code imports and uses MessageDigest with SHA-256, so MessageDigest alone is shared between noise and active code.

The javadoc anti-pattern block contains the full SQL-injection FP-triggering pattern: createStatement + st.executeQuery("SELECT ... " + req.getParameter). Pre-F10 the javadoc would induce the SQL rule to fire; post-F10 the javadoc is stripped and the active code binds parameters.

The javadoc anti-pattern block contains the full PATH-traversal FP-triggering pattern: new java.io.FileInputStream(new java.io.File("/var/templates/" + req.getParameter("file"))). Pre-F10 the javadoc would induce the path rule to fire; post-F10 the javadoc is stripped and the active code uses getResourceAsStream.

The javadoc anti-pattern block contains the full LDAP-injection FP-triggering pattern: new InitialDirContext().search(base, "(uid=" + req.getParameter("user") + ")", controls). Pre-F10 the javadoc would induce the LDAP rule to fire; post-F10 the javadoc is stripped and the active code returns a constant.
DES Cipher example appears only inside javadoc; the active code uses Cipher.getInstance with AES/GCM/NoPadding, so the bare Cipher.getInstance prefix is shared.
executeQuery appears in javadoc AND the active code builds a query via string concatenation from getParameter and calls executeQuery on it. F10 must preserve the active SQL injection.
MD5 token appears only inside a log-message string literal; the active code imports and calls MessageDigest with SHA-256.

The explanatory string literal contains the full SQL-injection FP-triggering pattern: Statement.executeQuery("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = " + req.getParameter("id")). Pre-F10 the literal would induce the SQL rule to fire; post-F10 the literal is stripped and the active code performs no SQL.
Math.random() phrase appears only in an exception message; the active code uses SecureRandom.

The user-facing suggestion string literal contains the full CMD-injection FP-triggering pattern: new ProcessBuilder().command("sh", "-c", "ls " + req.getParameter("dir")).start() and Runtime.getRuntime().exec mention. Pre-F10 the literal would induce the CMD rule to fire; post-F10 the literal is stripped and the active code returns a status enum.

The validation message string literal contains the full PATH-traversal FP-triggering pattern: new java.io.File("../" + req.getParameter("file")). Pre-F10 the literal would induce the path rule to fire; post-F10 the literal is stripped and the active code is a pure string check.
Math.random( appears in a string literal AND the active code uses new java.util.Random() to draw a token. F10 must preserve the active Random call.
char literals 'M', 'D', '5' used as labels in a char-array; multi-char substring MD5 is never present in active source.
char literals '/' and '\' used as path-separator constants; no java.io.File call exists.
char literals 'D' 'E' 'S' enumerated in an algorithm-name parser; no Cipher.getInstance call.
char literals ',', ';' used as CSV delimiters; no SQL execution.
char literals '?', '%' used as format-spec markers; no SQL execution.
char literals '/' '\\' used nearby AND active code calls new java.io.File(getParameter(...) + slash). F10 must preserve the active path traversal.

The Java 13+ text block contains the full SQL-injection FP-triggering pattern: createStatement + st.executeQuery("SELECT name FROM accounts WHERE id = '" + req.getParameter("id") + "'"). Pre-F10 the text block would induce the SQL rule to fire; post-F10 the text block is stripped and the active code binds parameters via PreparedStatement.
MD5 example appears only inside a text block treated as a JSON template; the active code imports and calls MessageDigest with SHA-256.

The Java 13+ text block contains the full XPath-injection FP-triggering pattern: XPathFactory.newInstance().newXPath().compile("//user[name='" + req.getParameter("name") + "']").evaluate(doc). Pre-F10 the text block would induce the XPath rule to fire; post-F10 the text block is stripped and the active code returns a static label.

The Java 13+ text block contains the full LDAP-injection FP-triggering pattern: new InitialDirContext().search(base, "(uid=" + req.getParameter("user") + ")", controls). Pre-F10 the text block would induce the LDAP rule to fire; post-F10 the text block is stripped and the active code returns a constant boolean.

The Java 13+ text block contains the full CMD-injection FP-triggering pattern: Runtime.getRuntime().exec("/bin/sh -c " + req.getParameter("cmd")) and new ProcessBuilder("/bin/sh", "-c", "ls " + req.getParameter("dir")).start(). Pre-F10 the text block would induce the CMD rule to fire; post-F10 the text block is stripped and the active code returns a constant string.
XPathFactory.newInstance( appears in a text block AND the active code builds an XPath expression from getParameter and calls evaluate. F10 must preserve the active XPath injection.
